item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President presently states the order’s administrative purpose and defines terms governing intelligence organizations; these provisions frame later internal executive operations rather than independently changing substantive legal rights.","evidence":"For the purpose of this Order, unless otherwise indicated, the following terms shall have these meanings"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The National Security Council must provide ongoing guidance and direction for developing intelligence activities, an internal executive-management function with no dictated legal consequence.","evidence":"shall provide guidance and direction to the development and formulation of national intelligence activities"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The National Security Council must periodically review intelligence policies and programs; the required result is administrative evaluation, not a specified legal outcome.","evidence":"shall conduct a semi-annual review of intelligence policies"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The National Security Council must consult designated officials, while the President immediately creates and staffs an internal committee; both are executive organization and coordination measures.","evidence":"There is established the Committee on Foreign Intelligence"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The CFI receives mandatory internal budgeting, policy, guidance, and reporting responsibilities, but retains discretion over amendments and reprogramming rules and is not directed to impose a specified external legal consequence.","evidence":"review, and amend as it deems appropriate, the budget for the National Foreign Intelligence Program"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The President organizes the Operations Group and assigns it internal advisory, review, and operational-approval functions; any operational consequence depends on later group decisions.","evidence":"There is established the Operations Advisory Group"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The Director of Central Intelligence receives internal leadership, advisory, procedural, oversight, coordination, and discretionary implementation duties rather than a mandated substantive legal outcome.","evidence":"Establish procedures to ensure the propriety of requests, and responses thereto"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The President establishes an internal deputy position and directs delegation and information access among executive officials, all immediate organizational or management measures.","evidence":"the position of Deputy to the Director of Central Intelligence for the Intelligence Community is hereby established"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads and the DCI must provide and safeguard intelligence information, followed by administrative scope and implementation rules; these regulate internal executive operations.","evidence":"Relevant information requested by the DCI shall be provided"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"Senior intelligence officials must administer their existing duties responsively to executive-branch needs, an ongoing internal management obligation.","evidence":"shall ensure that, in discharging the duties and responsibilities enumerated for their organizations"},{"segment_id":"11","code":2,"rationale":"Although most duties concern internal intelligence administration, senior officials are also required later to declassify qualifying material, a specified legally consequential information-status result produced through agency action.","evidence":"promptly declassifying such material consistent with Executive Order No. 11652, as amended"},{"segment_id":"12","code":1,"rationale":"The CIA and department heads are assigned investigations, support, collection, production, coordination, and intelligence-program functions; these are operational and administrative directions without a dictated later legal-rights result.","evidence":"Conduct administrative, technical and support activities in the United States or abroad"},{"segment_id":"13","code":3,"rationale":"After assigning internal intelligence functions, the segment itself presently prohibits foreign intelligence agencies from specified surveillance, searches, mail opening, tax-information examination, infiltration, and collection, immediately limiting governmental authority and protecting affected persons.","evidence":"Foreign intelligence agencies shall not engage in any of the following activities"}]}
